title: Exploring Speech Foundation Models for Speaker Diarization Across Lifespan
summary: Speech foundation models have shown strong transferability across a wide range of speech applications. However, their robustness to age-related domain shift in speaker diarization remains underexplored. In this work, we present a cross-lifespan evaluation within a unified end-to-end neural diarization framework (EEND-VC), covering speech samples from conversations involving children, adults, and older adults. We compare models under zero-shot cross-age inference, joint multi-age training, and domain-specific adaptation. Results show substantial performance degradation when models trained on adult-specific speech are applied to child and older-adult conversational data. Moreover, joint multi-age training across different age groups improves robustness without reducing diarization performance in canonical adult conversations, while targeted age group adaptation yields further gains in diarization performance, particularly when using the Whisper encoder.

AI.tldr: EEND-VC framework evaluation reveals speech foundation models degrade on age-related domain shifts in diarization; joint multi-age training improves robustness without harming adult performance, with Whisper encoder adaptation yielding best results.
AI.motivation: Speech foundation models demonstrate strong transferability across applications but their robustness to age-related domain shifts in speaker diarization remains underexplored, particularly for conversations involving children and older adults.
AI.method: Cross-lifespan evaluation within unified end-to-end neural diarization framework (EEND-VC), covering children, adults, and older adults. Comparison of zero-shot cross-age inference, joint multi-age training, and domain-specific adaptation strategies.
AI.result: Substantial performance degradation when adult-trained models applied to child/older-adult data. Joint multi-age training improves robustness without reducing diarization performance in canonical adult conversations. Targeted age group adaptation yields further gains, particularly with Whisper encoder.
AI.conclusion: Age-related domain shift significantly impacts speaker diarization performance; joint multi-age training enhances robustness across lifespan while maintaining adult performance; domain-specific adaptation with Whisper encoder provides optimal diarization improvements for non-adult age groups.

title: Active noise cancellation on open-ear smart glasses
summary: Smart glasses are becoming an increasingly prevalent wearable platform, with audio as a key interaction modality. However, hearing in noisy environments remains challenging because smart glasses are equipped with open-ear speakers that do not seal the ear canal. Furthermore, the open-ear design is incompatible with conventional active noise cancellation (ANC) techniques, which rely on an error microphone inside or at the entrance of the ear canal to measure the residual sound heard after cancellation. Here we present the first real-time ANC system for open-ear smart glasses that suppresses environmental noise using only microphones and miniaturized open-ear speakers embedded in the glasses frame. Our low-latency computational pipeline estimates the noise at the ear from an array of eight microphones distributed around the glasses frame and generates an anti-noise signal in real-time to cancel environmental noise. We develop a custom glasses prototype and evaluate it in a user study across 8 environments under mobility in the 100--1000 Hz frequency range, where environmental noise is concentrated. We achieve a mean noise reduction of 9.6 dB without any calibration, and 11.2 dB with a brief user-specific calibration.

AI.tldr: First real-time ANC system for open-ear smart glasses using only onboard microphones and speakers, achieving 9.6-11.2 dB noise reduction in 100-1000 Hz range without ear canal sealing.
AI.motivation: Smart glasses with open-ear speakers face hearing challenges in noisy environments because they don't seal the ear canal, making them incompatible with conventional ANC techniques that require error microphones inside or at the ear canal entrance.
AI.method: Developed a low-latency computational pipeline that estimates noise at the ear from an array of eight microphones distributed around the glasses frame and generates anti-noise signals in real-time. Built a custom glasses prototype and evaluated it across 8 environments under mobility conditions.
AI.result: Achieved mean noise reduction of 9.6 dB without calibration and 11.2 dB with brief user-specific calibration in the 100-1000 Hz frequency range where environmental noise is concentrated.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrated the first real-time ANC system for open-ear smart glasses that effectively suppresses environmental noise without requiring ear canal sealing, enabling better audio interaction in noisy environments.

title: Multimodal Deep Learning Method for Real-Time Spatial Room Impulse Response Computing
comment: This work was accepted by ICASSP 2026
summary: We propose a multimodal deep learning model for VR auralization that generates spatial room impulse responses (SRIRs) in real time to reconstruct scene-specific auditory perception. Employing SRIRs as the output reduces computational complexity and facilitates integration with personalized head-related transfer functions. The model takes two modalities as input: scene information and waveforms, where the waveform corresponds to the low-order reflections (LoR). LoR can be efficiently computed using geometrical acoustics (GA) but remains difficult for deep learning models to predict accurately. Scene geometry, acoustic properties, source coordinates, and listener coordinates are first used to compute LoR in real time via GA, and both LoR and these features are subsequently provided as inputs to the model. A new dataset was constructed, consisting of multiple scenes and their corresponding SRIRs. The dataset exhibits greater diversity. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed model.

AI.tldr: A multimodal deep learning model for real-time VR auralization that generates spatial room impulse responses using scene information and pre-computed low-order reflections as inputs, achieving superior performance with reduced computational complexity.
AI.motivation: To enable real-time, scene-specific auditory perception in VR with reduced computational complexity by leveraging multimodal inputs and separating the prediction of computationally intensive components from deep learning tasks.
AI.method: Multimodal deep learning model that takes two inputs: 1) scene information (geometry, acoustic properties, source/listener coordinates) and 2) pre-computed low-order reflection waveforms via geometrical acoustics. The model generates spatial room impulse responses as output, facilitating integration with personalized HRTFs.
AI.result: Experimental results demonstrate superior performance of the proposed model. A new diverse dataset was constructed with multiple scenes and corresponding SRIRs to support training and evaluation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed multimodal approach effectively combines efficient geometrical acoustics computation for low-order reflections with deep learning for SRIR generation, enabling real-time VR auralization with scene-specific auditory perception while reducing computational complexity.

title: Generalizable Audio-Visual Navigation via Binaural Difference Attention and Action Transition Prediction
comment: Main paper (6 pages). Accepted for publication by the International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN 2026)
summary: In Audio-Visual Navigation (AVN), agents must locate sound sources in unseen 3D environments using visual and auditory cues. However, existing methods often struggle with generalization in unseen scenarios, as they tend to overfit to semantic sound features and specific training environments. To address these challenges, we propose the \textbf{Binaural Difference Attention with Action Transition Prediction (BDATP)} framework, which jointly optimizes perception and policy. Specifically, the \textbf{Binaural Difference Attention (BDA)} module explicitly models interaural differences to enhance spatial orientation, reducing reliance on semantic categories. Simultaneously, the \textbf{Action Transition Prediction (ATP)} task introduces an auxiliary action prediction objective as a regularization term, mitigating environment-specific overfitting. Extensive experiments on the Replica and Matterport3D datasets demonstrate that BDATP can be seamlessly integrated into various mainstream baselines, yielding consistent and significant performance gains. Notably, our framework achieves state-of-the-art Success Rates across most settings, with a remarkable absolute improvement of up to 21.6 percentage points in Replica dataset for unheard sounds. These results underscore BDATP's superior generalization capability and its robustness across diverse navigation architectures.

AI.tldr: BDATP framework improves audio-visual navigation generalization by modeling binaural differences for spatial orientation and using action transition prediction to prevent overfitting, achieving state-of-the-art performance with up to 21.6% improvement on unheard sounds.
AI.motivation: Existing audio-visual navigation methods struggle with generalization in unseen scenarios due to overfitting to semantic sound features and specific training environments, limiting their practical applicability.
AI.method: Proposes BDATP framework with two components: 1) Binaural Difference Attention (BDA) module that explicitly models interaural differences to enhance spatial orientation and reduce reliance on semantic categories, and 2) Action Transition Prediction (ATP) task that introduces an auxiliary action prediction objective as a regularization term to mitigate environment-specific overfitting.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on Replica and Matterport3D datasets show BDATP can be seamlessly integrated into various mainstream baselines, yielding consistent and significant performance gains. Achieves state-of-the-art Success Rates across most settings, with absolute improvement of up to 21.6 percentage points in Replica dataset for unheard sounds.
AI.conclusion: BDATP demonstrates superior generalization capability and robustness across diverse navigation architectures by jointly optimizing perception and policy through explicit spatial modeling and regularization techniques.

title: Learning Kalman Policy for Singular Unknown Covariances via Riemannian Regularization
summary: Kalman filtering is a cornerstone of estimation theory, yet learning the optimal filter under unknown and potentially singular noise covariances remains a fundamental challenge. In this paper, we revisit this problem through the lens of control--estimation duality and data-driven policy optimization, formulating the learning of the steady-state Kalman gain as a stochastic policy optimization problem directly from measurement data. Our key contribution is a Riemannian regularization that reshapes the optimization landscape, restoring structural properties such as coercivity and gradient dominance. This geometric perspective enables the effective use of first-order methods under significantly relaxed conditions, including unknown and rank-deficient noise covariances. Building on this framework, we develop a computationally efficient algorithm with a data-driven gradient oracle, enabling scalable stochastic implementations. We further establish non-asymptotic convergence and error guarantees enabled by the Riemannian regularization, quantifying the impact of bias and variance in gradient estimates and demonstrating favorable scaling with problem dimension. Numerical results corroborate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and robustness to the choice of stepsize in challenging singular estimation regimes.

AI.tldr: Learning optimal Kalman filters under unknown/singular noise via control-estimation duality and Riemannian regularization for improved optimization landscape.
AI.motivation: Kalman filtering is fundamental but learning optimal filters under unknown and potentially singular noise covariances remains challenging, requiring new approaches that can handle these difficult estimation regimes.
AI.method: Formulates learning steady-state Kalman gain as stochastic policy optimization from measurement data using control-estimation duality. Introduces Riemannian regularization to reshape optimization landscape, restoring structural properties like coercivity and gradient dominance. Develops computationally efficient algorithm with data-driven gradient oracle for scalable stochastic implementations.
AI.result: Establishes non-asymptotic convergence and error guarantees enabled by Riemannian regularization, quantifying impact of bias/variance in gradient estimates with favorable scaling in problem dimension. Numerical results show effectiveness and robustness to stepsize choice in challenging singular estimation regimes.
AI.conclusion: Riemannian regularization enables effective first-order methods for learning Kalman filters under significantly relaxed conditions including unknown and rank-deficient noise covariances, providing a geometric perspective that restores desirable optimization properties.

title: YMIR: A new Benchmark Dataset and Model for Arabic Yemeni Music Genre Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: Automatic music genre classification is a major task in music information retrieval; however, most current benchmarks and models have been developed primarily for Western music, leaving culturally specific traditions underrepresented. In this paper, we introduce the Yemeni Music Information Retrieval (YMIR) dataset, which contains 1,475 carefully selected audio clips covering five traditional Yemeni genres: Sanaani, Hadhrami, Lahji, Tihami, and Adeni. The dataset was labeled by five Yemeni music experts following a clear and structured protocol, resulting in strong inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss kappa = 0.85). We also propose the Yemeni Music Classification Model (YMCM), a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based system designed to classify music genres from time-frequency features. Using a consistent preprocessing pipeline, we perform a systematic comparison across six experimental groups and five different architectures, resulting in a total of 30 experiments. Specifically, we evaluate several feature representations, including Mel-spectrograms, Chroma, FilterBank, and MFCCs with 13, 20, and 40 coefficients, and benchmark YMCM against standard models (AlexNet, VGG16, MobileNet, and a baseline CNN) under the same experimental conditions. The experimental findings reveal that YMCM is the most effective, achieving the highest accuracy of 98.8% with Mel-spectrogram features. The results also provide practical insights into the relationship between feature representation and model capacity. The findings establish YMIR as a useful benchmark and YMCM as a strong baseline for classifying Yemeni music genres.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces YMIR, the first dataset for Yemeni music genre classification, and proposes YMCM, a CNN-based model that achieves 98.8% accuracy on this dataset, establishing benchmarks for culturally specific music analysis.
AI.motivation: Current music genre classification benchmarks and models are primarily developed for Western music, leaving culturally specific traditions like Yemeni music underrepresented in music information retrieval research.
AI.method: Created YMIR dataset with 1,475 audio clips across 5 traditional Yemeni genres, labeled by 5 experts with strong inter-annotator agreement. Proposed YMCM, a CNN-based system, and conducted systematic comparison across 6 experimental groups and 5 architectures (30 total experiments) using various feature representations including Mel-spectrograms, Chroma, FilterBank, and MFCCs with different coefficients.
AI.result: YMCM achieved the highest accuracy of 98.8% using Mel-spectrogram features. The systematic comparison revealed YMCM's superiority over standard models (AlexNet, VGG16, MobileNet, baseline CNN) under the same experimental conditions.
AI.conclusion: The YMIR dataset serves as a valuable benchmark for Yemeni music genre classification, and YMCM establishes a strong baseline model. The research provides practical insights into feature representation and model capacity relationships for culturally specific music analysis.

title: Scalar Federated Learning for Linear Quadratic Regulator
summary: We propose ScalarFedLQR, a communication-efficient federated algorithm for model-free learning of a common policy in linear quadratic regulator (LQR) control of heterogeneous agents. The method builds on a decomposed projected gradient mechanism, in which each agent communicates only a scalar projection of a local zeroth-order gradient estimate. The server aggregates these scalar messages to reconstruct a global descent direction, reducing per-agent uplink communication from O(d) to O(1), independent of the policy dimension. Crucially, the projection-induced approximation error diminishes as the number of participating agents increases, yielding a favorable scaling law: larger fleets enable more accurate gradient recovery, admit larger stepsizes, and achieve faster linear convergence despite high dimensionality. Under standard regularity conditions, all iterates remain stabilizing and the average LQR cost decreases linearly fast. Numerical results demonstrate performance comparable to full-gradient federated LQR with substantially reduced communication.

AI.tldr: ScalarFedLQR is a communication-efficient federated algorithm for model-free LQR control that reduces per-agent uplink communication from O(d) to O(1) by having agents communicate only scalar projections of local gradient estimates.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address the communication bottleneck in federated learning for LQR control, particularly for high-dimensional policies where traditional methods require O(d) communication per agent, which becomes prohibitive for large fleets of heterogeneous agents.
AI.method: The method uses a decomposed projected gradient mechanism where each agent computes a local zeroth-order gradient estimate, projects it to a scalar, and communicates only this scalar to the server. The server aggregates these scalar messages to reconstruct a global descent direction for policy updates.
AI.result: The algorithm achieves linear convergence under standard regularity conditions, with all iterates remaining stabilizing and average LQR cost decreasing linearly fast. Numerical results show performance comparable to full-gradient federated LQR with substantially reduced communication overhead.
AI.conclusion: ScalarFedLQR enables efficient federated learning for LQR control by exploiting fleet size to overcome dimensionality challenges - larger fleets enable more accurate gradient recovery, admit larger stepsizes, and achieve faster convergence despite high-dimensional policies.

title: Anchored Cyclic Generation: A Novel Paradigm for Long-Sequence Symbolic Music Generation
summary: Generating long sequences with structural coherence remains a fundamental challenge for autoregressive models across sequential generation tasks. In symbolic music generation, this challenge is particularly pronounced, as existing methods are constrained by the inherent severe error accumulation problem of autoregressive models, leading to poor performance in music quality and structural integrity. In this paper, we propose the Anchored Cyclic Generation (ACG) paradigm, which relies on anchor features from already identified music to guide subsequent generation during the autoregressive process, effectively mitigating error accumulation in autoregressive methods. Based on the ACG paradigm, we further propose the Hierarchical Anchored Cyclic Generation (Hi-ACG) framework, which employs a systematic global-to-local generation strategy and is highly compatible with our specifically designed piano token, an efficient musical representation. The experimental results demonstrate that compared to traditional autoregressive models, the ACG paradigm achieves reduces cosine distance by an average of 34.7% between predicted feature vectors and ground-truth semantic vectors. In long-sequence symbolic music generation tasks, the Hi-ACG framework significantly outperforms existing mainstream methods in both subjective and objective evaluations. Furthermore, the framework exhibits excellent task generalization capabilities, achieving superior performance in related tasks such as music completion.

AI.tldr: ACG paradigm uses anchor features to guide autoregressive generation, reducing error accumulation; Hi-ACG framework employs hierarchical global-to-local strategy with piano token representation, outperforming existing methods in music generation tasks.
AI.motivation: Autoregressive models struggle with generating long sequences with structural coherence, especially in symbolic music generation where error accumulation severely impacts music quality and structural integrity.
AI.method: Proposes Anchored Cyclic Generation (ACG) paradigm using anchor features from identified music to guide subsequent generation, mitigating error accumulation. Extends to Hierarchical Anchored Cyclic Generation (Hi-ACG) with global-to-local strategy and piano token representation.
AI.result: ACG reduces cosine distance by 34.7% between predicted and ground-truth semantic vectors. Hi-ACG significantly outperforms existing methods in both subjective and objective evaluations for long-sequence symbolic music generation, with excellent generalization to tasks like music completion.
AI.conclusion: The ACG paradigm and Hi-ACG framework effectively address error accumulation in autoregressive models for symbolic music generation, improving structural coherence and music quality while demonstrating strong generalization capabilities.

title: Finite-Step Invariant Sets for Hybrid Systems with Probabilistic Guarantees
summary: Poincare return maps are a fundamental tool for analyzing periodic orbits in hybrid dynamical systems, including legged locomotion, power electronics, and other cyber-physical systems with switching behavior. The Poincare return map captures the evolution of the hybrid system on a guard surface, reducing the stability analysis of a periodic orbit to that of a discrete-time system. While linearization provides local stability information, assessing robustness to disturbances requires identifying invariant sets of the state space under the return dynamics. However, computing such invariant sets is computationally difficult, especially when system dynamics are only available through forward simulation. In this work, we propose an algorithmic framework leveraging sampling-based optimization to compute a finite-step invariant ellipsoid around a nominal periodic orbit using sampled evaluations of the return map. The resulting solution is accompanied by probabilistic guarantees on finite-step invariance satisfying a user-defined accuracy threshold. We demonstrate the approach on two low-dimensional systems and a compass-gait walking model.

AI.tldr: Algorithmic framework using sampling-based optimization to compute finite-step invariant ellipsoids around periodic orbits in hybrid systems, with probabilistic guarantees on invariance accuracy.
AI.motivation: Poincare return maps are essential for analyzing periodic orbits in hybrid systems, but computing invariant sets for robustness assessment is computationally difficult, especially when dynamics are only available through forward simulation.
AI.method: Proposes a sampling-based optimization framework that computes finite-step invariant ellipsoids around nominal periodic orbits using sampled evaluations of the Poincare return map.
AI.result: The approach provides solutions with probabilistic guarantees on finite-step invariance satisfying user-defined accuracy thresholds, demonstrated on two low-dimensional systems and a compass-gait walking model.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables computationally tractable computation of invariant sets for hybrid systems with simulation-only dynamics, offering probabilistic guarantees for robustness analysis of periodic orbits.

title: Controllable Singing Style Conversion with Boundary-Aware Information Bottleneck
summary: This paper presents the submission of the S4 team to the Singing Voice Conversion Challenge 2025 (SVCC2025)-a novel singing style conversion system that advances fine-grained style conversion and control within in-domain settings. To address the critical challenges of style leakage, dynamic rendering, and high-fidelity generation with limited data, we introduce three key innovations: a boundary-aware Whisper bottleneck that pools phoneme-span representations to suppress residual source style while preserving linguistic content; an explicit frame-level technique matrix, enhanced by targeted F0 processing during inference, for stable and distinct dynamic style rendering; and a perceptually motivated high-frequency band completion strategy that leverages an auxiliary standard 48kHz SVC model to augment the high-frequency spectrum, thereby overcoming data scarcity without overfitting. In the official SVCC2025 subjective evaluation, our system achieves the best naturalness performance among all submissions while maintaining competitive results in speaker similarity and technique control, despite using significantly less extra singing data than other top-performing systems. Audio samples are available online.

AI.tldr: S4 team's SVCC2025 submission introduces a novel singing style conversion system with three key innovations for fine-grained style control, addressing style leakage, dynamic rendering, and high-fidelity generation with limited data.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses critical challenges in singing voice conversion: style leakage (residual source style contamination), dynamic rendering difficulties, and high-fidelity generation with limited training data. These issues are particularly important for in-domain singing style conversion where fine-grained control is needed.
AI.method: Three key innovations: 1) Boundary-aware Whisper bottleneck that pools phoneme-span representations to suppress source style while preserving linguistic content; 2) Explicit frame-level technique matrix enhanced by targeted F0 processing during inference for stable dynamic style rendering; 3) Perceptually motivated high-frequency band completion strategy using an auxiliary 48kHz SVC model to augment high-frequency spectrum without overfitting.
AI.result: In official SVCC2025 subjective evaluation, the system achieved best naturalness performance among all submissions while maintaining competitive results in speaker similarity and technique control, despite using significantly less extra singing data than other top-performing systems.
AI.conclusion: The proposed system successfully addresses key challenges in singing style conversion through targeted architectural innovations, demonstrating that high-quality style conversion can be achieved with limited data through careful design of style separation, dynamic control, and frequency enhancement components.

title: Differentiable Invariant Sets for Hybrid Limit Cycles with Application to Legged Robots
summary: For hybrid systems exhibiting periodic behavior, analyzing the invariant set containing the limit cycle is a natural way to study the robustness of the closed-loop system. However, computing these sets can be computationally expensive, especially when applied to contact-rich cyber-physical systems such as legged robots. In this work, we extend existing methods for overapproximating reachable sets of continuous systems using parametric embeddings to compute a forward-invariant set around the nominal trajectory of a simplified model of a bipedal robot. Our three-step approach (i) computes an overapproximating reachable set around the nominal continuous flow, (ii) catalogs intersections with the guard surface, and (iii) passes these intersections through the reset map. If the overapproximated reachable set after one step is a strict subset of the initial set, we formally verify a forward invariant set for this hybrid periodic orbit. We verify this condition on the bipedal walker model numerically using immrax, a JAX-based library for parametric reachable set computation, and use it within a bi-level optimization framework to design a tracking controller that maximizes the size of the invariant set.

AI.tldr: Extends parametric reachable set methods to compute forward-invariant sets around limit cycles for hybrid systems, applied to bipedal walking verification and controller design.
AI.motivation: Analyzing invariant sets around limit cycles is crucial for studying robustness of periodic hybrid systems, but computation is expensive for contact-rich systems like legged robots.
AI.method: Three-step approach: (1) compute overapproximating reachable set around nominal continuous flow, (2) catalog intersections with guard surfaces, (3) pass intersections through reset maps. Uses parametric embeddings and immrax (JAX-based library) for numerical verification.
AI.result: Successfully verifies forward invariant sets for bipedal walker model numerically, and uses bi-level optimization to design tracking controllers that maximize invariant set size.
AI.conclusion: Method enables formal verification of forward invariant sets for hybrid periodic orbits and supports controller design for robustness maximization in contact-rich cyber-physical systems.

title: Time-Domain Voice Identity Morphing (TD-VIM): A Signal-Level Approach to Morphing Attacks on Speaker Verification Systems
summary: In biometric systems, it is a common practice to associate each sample or template with a specific individual. Nevertheless, recent studies have demonstrated the feasibility of generating "morphed" biometric samples capable of matching multiple identities. These morph attacks have been recognized as potential security risks for biometric systems. However, most research on morph attacks has focused on biometric modalities that operate within the image domain, such as the face, fingerprints, and iris. In this work, we introduce Time-domain Voice Identity Morphing (TD-VIM), a novel approach for voice-based biometric morphing. This method enables the blending of voice characteristics from two distinct identities at the signal level, creating morphed samples that present a high vulnerability for speaker verification systems. Leveraging the Multilingual Audio-Visual Smartphone database, our study created four distinct morphed signals based on morphing factors and evaluated their effectiveness using a comprehensive vulnerability analysis. To assess the security impact of TD-VIM, we benchmarked our approach using the Generalized Morphing Attack Potential (G-MAP) metric, measuring attack success across two deep-learning-based Speaker Verification Systems (SVS) and one commercial system, Verispeak. Our findings indicate that the morphed voice samples achieved a high attack success rate, with G-MAP values reaching 99.40% on iPhone-11 and 99.74% on Samsung S8 in text-dependent scenarios, at a false match rate of 0.1%.

AI.tldr: TD-VIM introduces time-domain voice identity morphing to create voice samples that can match multiple identities, demonstrating high vulnerability in speaker verification systems with G-MAP values up to 99.74%.
AI.motivation: While morph attacks have been studied for image-based biometrics (face, fingerprints, iris), voice-based biometric morphing remains underexplored despite the security risks posed by morphed samples that can match multiple identities in verification systems.
AI.method: Time-domain Voice Identity Morphing (TD-VIM) blends voice characteristics from two distinct identities at the signal level. The study used the Multilingual Audio-Visual Smartphone database to create four distinct morphed signals based on morphing factors, then evaluated vulnerability using Generalized Morphing Attack Potential (G-MAP) metric across two deep-learning-based SVS and one commercial system (Verispeak).
AI.result: Morphed voice samples achieved high attack success rates with G-MAP values reaching 99.40% on iPhone-11 and 99.74% on Samsung S8 in text-dependent scenarios at a false match rate of 0.1%, demonstrating significant vulnerability in speaker verification systems.
AI.conclusion: TD-VIM represents a novel and effective voice-based biometric morphing approach that poses serious security risks to speaker verification systems, highlighting the need for improved countermeasures against voice morphing attacks.

title: Synchronous Observer Design for Landmark-Inertial SLAM with Magnetometer and Intermittent GNSS Measurements
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, This work has been submitted to CDC 2026
summary: In Landmark-Inertial Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping (LI-SLAM), the positions of landmarks in the environment and the robot's pose relative to these landmarks are estimated using landmark position measurements, and measurements from the Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU). However, the robot and landmark positions in the inertial frame, and the yaw of the robot, are not observable in LI-SLAM. This paper proposes a nonlinear observer for LI-SLAM that overcomes the observability constraints with the addition of intermittent GNSS position and magnetometer measurements. The full-state error dynamics of the proposed observer is shown to be both almost-globally asymptotically stable and locally exponentially stable, and this is validated using simulations.

AI.tldr: Proposes a nonlinear observer for Landmark-Inertial SLAM that overcomes observability limitations by incorporating intermittent GNSS and magnetometer measurements, achieving almost-global asymptotic and local exponential stability.
AI.motivation: LI-SLAM suffers from unobservability of robot/landmark positions in inertial frame and robot yaw due to inherent observability constraints, limiting its practical applications.
AI.method: Develops a nonlinear observer that integrates intermittent GNSS position measurements and magnetometer readings with standard LI-SLAM to address observability issues.
AI.result: The proposed observer achieves almost-globally asymptotically stable and locally exponentially stable full-state error dynamics, validated through simulations.
AI.conclusion: Intermittent GNSS and magnetometer measurements effectively resolve observability constraints in LI-SLAM, enabling robust estimation of previously unobservable states.

title: Generating Synthetic Doctor-Patient Conversations for Long-form Audio Summarization
summary: Long-context audio reasoning is underserved in both training data and evaluation. Existing benchmarks target short-context tasks, and the open-ended generation tasks most relevant to long-context reasoning pose well-known challenges for automatic evaluation. We propose a synthetic data generation pipeline designed to serve both as a training resource and as a controlled evaluation environment, and instantiate it for first-visit doctor-patient conversations with SOAP note generation as the task. The pipeline has three stages, persona-driven dialogue generation, multi-speaker audio synthesis with overlap/pause modeling, room acoustics, and sound events, and LLM-based reference SOAP note production, built entirely on open-weight models. We release 8,800 synthetic conversations with 1.3k hours of corresponding audio and reference notes. Evaluating current open-weight systems, we find that cascaded approaches still substantially outperform end-to-end models.

AI.tldr: Proposes synthetic data pipeline for long-context audio reasoning, creating 8,800 doctor-patient conversations with 1.3k hours of audio and SOAP notes for training/evaluation, showing cascaded approaches outperform end-to-end models.
AI.motivation: Long-context audio reasoning lacks adequate training data and evaluation benchmarks; existing benchmarks focus on short-context tasks, and open-ended generation tasks relevant to long-context reasoning face challenges in automatic evaluation.
AI.method: Three-stage synthetic data pipeline: 1) persona-driven dialogue generation, 2) multi-speaker audio synthesis with overlap/pause modeling, room acoustics, and sound events, 3) LLM-based reference SOAP note production, built entirely on open-weight models.
AI.result: Released 8,800 synthetic conversations with 1.3k hours of corresponding audio and reference notes; evaluation of current open-weight systems shows cascaded approaches substantially outperform end-to-end models.
AI.conclusion: The proposed synthetic data pipeline addresses the gap in long-context audio reasoning resources, providing both training data and controlled evaluation environment, with cascaded systems demonstrating superior performance over end-to-end approaches.

title: Reasoning about Parameters in the Friedkin--Johnsen Model from Binary Observations
summary: We consider a verification problem for opinion dynamics based on binary observations. The opinion dynamics is governed by a Friedkin-Johnsen (FJ) model, where only a sequence of binary outputs is available instead of the agents' continuous opinions. Specifically, at every time-step we observe a binarized output for each agent depending on whether the opinion exceeds a fixed threshold. The objective is to verify whether an FJ model with a given set of stubbornness parameters and initial opinions is consistent with the observed binary outputs up to a small error. The FJ model is formulated as a transition system, and an approximate simulation relation of two transition systems is defined in terms of the proximity of their opinion trajectories and output sequences. We then construct a finite set of abstract FJ models by simplifying the influence matrix and discretizing the stubbornness parameters and the initial opinions. It is shown that the abstraction approximately simulates any concrete FJ model with continuous parameters and initial opinions, and is itself approximately simulated by some concrete FJ model. These results ensure that consistency verification can be performed over the finite abstraction. Specifically, by checking whether an abstract model satisfies the observation constraints, we can conclude whether the corresponding family of concrete FJ models is consistent with the binary observations. Finally, numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the proposed verification framework.

AI.tldr: Verification of Friedkin-Johnsen opinion dynamics using only binary observations via finite abstraction and approximate simulation relations.
AI.motivation: Need to verify if an FJ model with specific parameters is consistent with observed binary outputs when only threshold-based binary observations are available instead of continuous opinions.
AI.method: Formulate FJ model as transition system, define approximate simulation relation, construct finite abstraction by simplifying influence matrix and discretizing parameters/initial opinions, then verify consistency over abstraction.
AI.result: The abstraction approximately simulates any concrete FJ model and vice versa, enabling consistency verification over finite abstraction by checking if abstract models satisfy observation constraints.
AI.conclusion: Proposed framework allows verification of FJ model consistency with binary observations using finite abstractions, demonstrated through numerical experiments.

title: Price-Coordinated Mean Field Games with State Augmentation for Decentralized Battery Charging
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to the 64th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC 2026)
summary: This paper addresses the decentralized coordinated charging problem for a large population of battery storage agents (e.g. residential batteries, electrical vehicles, charging station batteries) using Mean Field Game (MFG). Agents are assumed to have affine dynamics and are coupled through a price that is continuous and monotonically increasing with respect to the difference between the average charging power and the grid's desired average charging power. An important modeling feature of the proposed framework is the state augmentation, that is, the charging power is treated as a state variable and its rate of change (i.e. the ramp rate) as the control input. The resulting MFG equilibrium is characterized by two nonlinearly coupled forward-backward differential equations. The existence and uniqueness of the MFG equilibrium is established for any continuous and monotonically increasing nonlinear price function without additional restrictions on the time horizon. Moreover, in the special case where the price is affine in the average charging power, we further simplify the characterization of the MFG equilibrium strategy via two separate Riccati equations, both of which admit unique positive semi-definite solutions without additional assumptions.

AI.tldr: Decentralized coordinated charging for battery storage agents using Mean Field Game with state augmentation, establishing existence/uniqueness of equilibrium for monotonic price functions and simplified Riccati solutions for affine pricing.
AI.motivation: Address the decentralized coordinated charging problem for large populations of battery storage agents (residential batteries, EVs, charging stations) to manage grid stability and efficiency through price-based coordination.
AI.method: Use Mean Field Game framework with state augmentation (charging power as state, ramp rate as control), characterize equilibrium via coupled forward-backward differential equations, prove existence/uniqueness for monotonic price functions, and derive simplified Riccati equations for affine pricing case.
AI.result: Established existence and uniqueness of MFG equilibrium for any continuous monotonically increasing nonlinear price function without time horizon restrictions; for affine pricing, equilibrium strategy characterized via two separate Riccati equations with unique positive semi-definite solutions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed MFG framework with state augmentation effectively solves decentralized coordinated charging, providing theoretical guarantees for equilibrium existence/uniqueness and computationally tractable solutions for affine pricing scenarios.

title: An Ultra-Low-Power Synthesizable Asynchronous AER Encoder for Neuromorphic Edge Devices
summary: This paper presents a fully synthesizable, treebased Address-Event Representation (AER) encoder designed for scalable neuromorphic computing systems. To achieve high throughput while maintaining strict compatibility with commercial EDA workflows, the asynchronous design employs a bundled-data protocol within a semi-decoupled micropipeline. The architecture replaces traditional transparent latches with standard edge-triggered flip-flops, enabling digital synthesis and place-and-route (PnR) using Cadence toolkits. A cross-coupled NAND-based random-priority arbiter is embedded within the encoder of each tree node to resolve event collisions efficiently. An 8-event AER prototype is fabricated in 65 nm CMOS technology utilizing a purely digital standard-cell flow. Post-fabrication silicon measurements validate the design, demonstrating a peak throughput of 33 MEvent/s and an average event latency of 50 ns, equating to a propagation delay of 17 ns/(event-bit). The design consumes only 435 fJ per encoded event.

AI.tldr: A fully synthesizable tree-based AER encoder for neuromorphic systems achieves 33 MEvent/s throughput with 435 fJ/event using standard digital flow in 65nm CMOS.
AI.motivation: To create a scalable neuromorphic computing system component that is fully synthesizable and compatible with commercial EDA tools while maintaining high throughput for address-event representation encoding.
AI.method: Uses a tree-based architecture with bundled-data protocol in semi-decoupled micropipeline, replaces transparent latches with edge-triggered flip-flops for digital synthesis, incorporates cross-coupled NAND-based random-priority arbiters in each tree node, and implements in 65nm CMOS using standard-cell flow.
AI.result: Fabricated 8-event AER prototype demonstrates 33 MEvent/s peak throughput, 50 ns average event latency (17 ns/event-bit propagation delay), and 435 fJ per encoded event power consumption.
AI.conclusion: The design successfully achieves high-performance AER encoding with commercial EDA compatibility, demonstrating the feasibility of fully synthesizable neuromorphic components for scalable systems.

title: CT Saturation Detection and Compensation: A Hybrid Physical Model- and Data-Driven Method
summary: Current transformer (CT) saturation is one of the dominant causes of relay protection devices' malfunctions, which pose a threat to the safe operation of the power system. To address this problem, we propose a hybrid physical model- and data-driven method. The method firstly detects the CT saturation and then compensates it to reproduce the real waveform. Considering the multi-factor and strong nonlinearity of CT saturation, a data-driven model, namely the Fully Convolutional Network (FCN), is built to detect the operation status of CT. As for the compensation, a physical model of short-circuit current is used for its conciseness and universality. Through tactfully integrating the data model and the physical model, the proposed method is endowed with two major merits: the arduous adjustment of universal thresholds and parameters in existing methods is avoided, and the deficiency in generalization and interpretability of the data-driven method is assuaged. Simulation and experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Furthermore, its application potential to future protection is explored.

AI.tldr: Hybrid physical model- and data-driven method for CT saturation detection and compensation to prevent relay protection malfunctions in power systems.
AI.motivation: Current transformer (CT) saturation is a major cause of relay protection device malfunctions, threatening power system safety. Existing methods face challenges with threshold adjustment, generalization, and interpretability.
AI.method: Two-stage approach: 1) Data-driven Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) detects CT saturation status, addressing multi-factor nonlinearity; 2) Physical model of short-circuit current compensates saturation to reproduce real waveform. Hybrid integration combines strengths of both approaches.
AI.result: Simulation and experimental results verify method effectiveness. The approach avoids arduous threshold/parameter adjustments and improves generalization/interpretability compared to pure data-driven methods.
AI.conclusion: Proposed hybrid method effectively addresses CT saturation problems, shows application potential for future protection systems, and overcomes limitations of existing approaches through intelligent integration of physical and data-driven models.

title: To Defer or To Shift? The Role of AI Data Center Flexibility on Grid Interconnection
summary: The integration of AI data centers into power grid represents one of the most emerging and complex challenges for the energy systems. As computational demand scales at an unprecedented rate, the traditional grid planning study's paradigm of treating data centers as rigid, inflexible loads is becoming economically, mathematically and operationally untenable. This work tries to understand and address the large load interconnection bottleneck by modeling and evaluating AI load flexibility. By examining data center's temporal and spatial shifting capabilities within a grid capacity expansion framework, we build a quantitative grid planning model, and evaluate their impacts on additional generation, operational costs, and network congestion. Numerical study reveals interesting observations, as AI data center flexibility are not felt consistently, and increasing flexibility does not necessarily translate to less generation capacity required. Depending on data center's locations, flexibility range, and grid load conditions, flexible AI load can help reduce grid investment and operational costs by 3-21%. Our work also indicate that longer deferral time of AI compute has diminishing returns for offloading grid electricity dispatch pressure.

AI.tldr: AI data center flexibility modeling in grid planning shows 3-21% cost savings, but benefits vary with location, flexibility range, and grid conditions; longer compute deferral has diminishing returns.
AI.motivation: Traditional grid planning treats data centers as rigid loads, which is economically and operationally unsustainable given AI's unprecedented computational growth. There's a need to understand and address large load interconnection bottlenecks by modeling AI load flexibility.
AI.method: Developed a quantitative grid planning model examining data center temporal and spatial shifting capabilities within a grid capacity expansion framework. Evaluated impacts on generation, operational costs, and network congestion through numerical studies.
AI.result: AI data center flexibility benefits are inconsistent - increasing flexibility doesn't always reduce required generation capacity. Flexible AI loads can reduce grid investment and operational costs by 3-21%, depending on location, flexibility range, and grid conditions. Longer compute deferral has diminishing returns for relieving grid dispatch pressure.
AI.conclusion: AI data center flexibility modeling provides valuable insights for grid planning, showing potential cost savings but with context-dependent benefits. The diminishing returns of longer deferral times suggest optimal flexibility strategies need careful consideration of specific grid and data center characteristics.

title: Bridging Natural Language and Microgrid Dynamics: A Context-Aware Simulator and Dataset
summary: Addressing the critical need for intelligent, context-aware energy management in renewable systems, we introduce the \textbf{OpenCEM Simulator and Dataset}: the first open-source digital twin explicitly designed to integrate rich, unstructured contextual information with quantitative renewable energy dynamics. Traditional energy management relies heavily on numerical time series, thereby neglecting the significant predictive power embedded in human-generated context (e.g., event schedules, system logs, user intentions). OpenCEM bridges this gap by offering a unique platform comprising both a meticulously aligned, language-rich dataset from a real-world PV-and-battery microgrid installation and a modular simulator capable of natively processing this multi-modal context. The OpenCEM Simulator provides a high-fidelity environment for developing and validating novel control algorithms and prediction models, particularly those leveraging Large Language Models. We detail its component-based architecture, hybrid data-driven and physics-based modelling capabilities, and demonstrate its utility through practical examples, including context-aware load forecasting and the implementation of online optimal battery charging control strategies. By making this platform publicly available, OpenCEM aims to accelerate research into the next generation of intelligent, sustainable, and truly context-aware energy systems.

AI.tldr: OpenCEM introduces the first open-source digital twin platform integrating unstructured contextual information with renewable energy dynamics for intelligent, context-aware energy management.
AI.motivation: Traditional energy management relies heavily on numerical time series data, neglecting the predictive power of human-generated contextual information like event schedules, system logs, and user intentions. There's a critical need for intelligent, context-aware energy management in renewable systems that can leverage this rich contextual data.
AI.method: Developed OpenCEM Simulator and Dataset: an open-source digital twin platform with a modular simulator capable of natively processing multi-modal context, featuring component-based architecture and hybrid data-driven/physics-based modeling. Includes a meticulously aligned, language-rich dataset from a real-world PV-and-battery microgrid installation.
AI.result: Created a high-fidelity environment for developing and validating novel control algorithms and prediction models, particularly those leveraging Large Language Models. Demonstrated utility through practical examples including context-aware load forecasting and implementation of online optimal battery charging control strategies.
AI.conclusion: OpenCEM bridges the gap between traditional numerical approaches and context-aware energy management, accelerating research into next-generation intelligent, sustainable energy systems by making this platform publicly available.

title: An Additional Resonance Damping Control for Grey-Box D-PMSG Wind Farm Integrated Weak Grid
summary: Considerable efforts have been made to address the resonance issue of the Direct-drive Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (D-PMSG) wind farm integrated power systems. However, the D-PMSG controller structure and parameters are concealed because of commercial secrecy, thus the target system exhibits grey-box characteristics. The existing resonance damping methods are either unavailable for grey-box systems or economically infeasible, which makes resonance damping of grey-box systems extremely challenging. To address this issue, this paper proposes an Additional Resonance Damping Control (ARDC) specfically for the grey-box D-PMSG system. This strategy is achieved by incorporating an additional control loop outside the D-PMSG controller. Firstly, the external impedance characteristics are obtained by the frequency sweeping technique ofline and then the key parameter of the additional control loop is determined by the Bode-diagram-based method under the worst stability scenario. Once the resonance occurs, the external impedance of the black-box D-PMSG is reshaped online to increase the magnitude stability margin of the system, thus providing effective resonance damping. The ARDC's effectiveness is finally verfied in the simulation and controller-hardware-in-the-loop experiment under various operating conditions.

AI.tldr: Proposes Additional Resonance Damping Control (ARDC) for grey-box D-PMSG wind farm systems using external impedance reshaping to address resonance issues when controller parameters are concealed.
AI.motivation: D-PMSG wind farm systems suffer from resonance issues, but controller structures/parameters are concealed due to commercial secrecy (grey-box characteristics). Existing resonance damping methods are either unavailable for grey-box systems or economically infeasible.
AI.method: ARDC adds external control loop outside D-PMSG controller. Uses frequency sweeping offline to obtain external impedance characteristics, then determines key parameter via Bode-diagram method under worst stability scenario. When resonance occurs, reshapes external impedance online to increase magnitude stability margin.
AI.result: ARDC provides effective resonance damping for grey-box D-PMSG systems. Effectiveness verified through simulation and controller-hardware-in-the-loop experiments under various operating conditions.
AI.conclusion: Proposed ARDC strategy successfully addresses resonance damping challenges in grey-box D-PMSG wind farm systems by reshaping external impedance without requiring knowledge of concealed controller parameters.

title: Optimality Robustness in Koopman-Based Control
summary: The Koopman operator enables simplified representations for nonlinear systems in data-driven optimal control, but the accompanying uncertainties inevitably induce deviations in the optimal controller and associated value function. This raises a distinct and fundamental question on optimality robustness, specifically, how uncertainties affect the optimal solution itself. To address this problem, we adopt a unified analysis-to-design perspective for systematically quantifying and improving optimality robustness. At the analysis level, we derive explicit upper bounds on the deviations of both the value function and the optimal controller, where uncertainties from multiple sources are systematically integrated into a unified norm-bounded representation. At the design level, we develop a robustness-aware optimal control methodology that provably reduces such optimality deviations, thereby enhancing robustness while explicitly revealing a quantitative trade-off between nominal optimality and robustness. As for practical implementation aspect, we further propose a tractable policy iteration algorithm, whose well-posedness and convergence are established via vanishing viscosity regularization and elliptic partial differential equation (PDE) techniques. Numerical examples validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed methodology.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses optimality robustness in Koopman operator-based optimal control by quantifying uncertainty effects on optimal solutions and developing robustness-aware control methods with provable performance guarantees.
AI.motivation: Uncertainties in Koopman operator representations inevitably cause deviations in optimal controllers and value functions, raising fundamental questions about how uncertainties affect optimal solutions themselves and the need for systematic quantification and improvement of optimality robustness.
AI.method: Adopts unified analysis-to-design perspective: (1) Analysis level derives explicit upper bounds on value function and optimal controller deviations, integrating multiple uncertainty sources into unified norm-bounded representation; (2) Design level develops robustness-aware optimal control methodology that reduces optimality deviations; (3) Practical implementation proposes tractable policy iteration algorithm with well-posedness and convergence established via vanishing viscosity regularization and elliptic PDE techniques.
AI.result: Theoretical framework provides explicit quantification of optimality deviations, robustness-aware control methodology that provably reduces deviations, and practical algorithm with established convergence properties. Numerical examples validate theoretical findings and demonstrate methodology effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: The paper presents a systematic approach to optimality robustness in Koopman-based control, offering both analytical quantification tools and practical design methods that explicitly reveal the trade-off between nominal optimality and robustness, with validated effectiveness through numerical examples.

title: Predictor-Feedback CACC for Vehicular Platoons with Actuation and Communication Delays Based on a Multiple-Predecessor-Following CTH Nominal Strategy
summary: We develop a predictor-feedback cooperative adaptive cruise control (CACC) design relying on a multiple-predecessor-following (MPF) topology-based nominal delay-free CACC law. We consider vehicular platoons with heterogeneous vehicles, whose dynamics are described by a third-order linear system subject to actuation delay, along with vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication delay. The design achieves individual vehicle stability, string stability, and zero, steady-state speed/spacing tracking errors, for any value of the actuation delay. The proofs of individual vehicle stability, string stability, and regulation rely on employment of an input-output approach on the frequency domain, capitalizing on the delay-compensating property of the design, which enables as to derive explicit string stability conditions on control and vehicle models parameters. The theoretical guarantees of string stability and the respective conditions on parameters are illustrated also numerically. We present consistent simulation results, for a ten-vehicle platoon, illustrating the potential of the design in traffic throughput improvement, as compared with a predictor-feedback CACC design in which, each ego vehicle's controller utilizes information only from a single preceding vehicle. We also present simulation results in a realistic scenario in which the leading vehicle's trajectory is obtained from NGSIM data.

AI.tldr: Predictor-feedback CACC design using MPF topology achieves individual and string stability with zero steady-state errors despite actuation and communication delays.
AI.motivation: Address stability and performance challenges in heterogeneous vehicle platoons with both actuation and V2V communication delays, improving traffic throughput compared to single-predecessor designs.
AI.method: Develop predictor-feedback CACC design based on multiple-predecessor-following topology, using frequency-domain input-output analysis with delay compensation for third-order linear vehicle dynamics.
AI.result: Achieves individual vehicle stability, string stability, and zero steady-state speed/spacing tracking errors for any actuation delay value, with explicit string stability conditions on control parameters.
AI.conclusion: MPF-based predictor-feedback CACC outperforms single-predecessor designs in traffic throughput, validated through simulations including realistic NGSIM data scenarios.

title: Quantifying Control Performance Loss for a Least Significant Bits Authentication Scheme
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Accepted for 2026 24th European Control Conference (ECC)
summary: Industrial control systems (ICSs) often consist of many legacy devices, which were designed without security requirements in mind. With the increase in cyberattacks targeting critical infrastructure, there is a growing urgency to develop legacy-compatible security solutions tailored to the specific needs and constraints of real-time control systems. We propose a least significant bits (LSBs) coding scheme providing message authenticity and integrity, which is compatible with legacy devices and never compromises availability. The scheme comes with provable security guarantees, and we provide a simple yet effective method to deal with synchronization issues due to packet dropouts. Furthermore, we quantify the control performance loss for both a fixed-point and floating-point quantization architecture when using the proposed coding scheme. We demonstrate its effectiveness in detecting cyberattacks, as well as the impact on control performance, on a hydro power turbine control system.

AI.tldr: LSB coding scheme for ICS security that provides message authenticity/integrity while maintaining compatibility with legacy devices and ensuring availability, with provable security and synchronization handling.
AI.motivation: Industrial control systems contain legacy devices designed without security requirements, making them vulnerable to cyberattacks targeting critical infrastructure, creating urgent need for legacy-compatible security solutions for real-time control systems.
AI.method: Proposed a least significant bits (LSBs) coding scheme that provides message authenticity and integrity while maintaining compatibility with legacy devices. Includes provable security guarantees and a simple method to handle synchronization issues from packet dropouts. Analyzed control performance loss for both fixed-point and floating-point quantization architectures.
AI.result: Demonstrated effectiveness in detecting cyberattacks and quantified control performance impact on a hydro power turbine control system. The scheme maintains availability while providing security.
AI.conclusion: The LSB coding scheme offers a practical, legacy-compatible security solution for industrial control systems that balances security requirements with control performance constraints, addressing critical infrastructure protection needs.

title: Network Reconstruction in Consensus Algorithms with Hidden Agents
summary: Reconstructing the parameters that encode the influence between model variables based on time-series measurements represents an outstanding question in the theory of complex network-coupled systems. Here, we propose a solution to this problem for a class of noisy leader-follower consensus algorithm, where one has access to measurements only from the followers but not from the leaders. Leveraging the directed Laplacian coupling of such systems, we present an autoregressive expansion of the observed dynamics which can be truncated at different orders, depending on the memory of the leaders. When their memory is short, this allows one to correctly reconstruct the full dynamical matrix with hidden leader agents, provided some additional assumption on the system to lift the degeneracy in the reconstruction. We illustrate and check the theory using numerical simulations for the cases of both a single and multiple hidden leaders.

AI.tldr: Proposes method to reconstruct influence parameters in leader-follower consensus networks when only follower measurements are available, using autoregressive expansion and directed Laplacian coupling.
AI.motivation: Reconstructing influence parameters between model variables from time-series measurements is a fundamental challenge in complex network-coupled systems, particularly when only follower measurements are available while leaders remain hidden.
AI.method: Uses directed Laplacian coupling of noisy leader-follower consensus algorithms to develop an autoregressive expansion of observed follower dynamics. The expansion can be truncated based on leader memory length, enabling reconstruction of the full dynamical matrix with hidden leaders under certain assumptions to resolve degeneracy.
AI.result: When leader memory is short, the method correctly reconstructs the full dynamical matrix with hidden leader agents, provided additional system assumptions to lift reconstruction degeneracy. Numerical simulations validate the theory for both single and multiple hidden leader cases.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach successfully addresses the parameter reconstruction problem in leader-follower consensus networks with hidden leaders, providing a solution to the outstanding question of inferring influence parameters from partial time-series measurements in complex network-coupled systems.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Optimal Control for Precision Immobilization Technique in Emergency Scenarios
summary: Precision Immobilization Technique (PIT) is a potentially effective intervention maneuver for emergency out-of-control vehicle, but its automation is challenged by highly nonlinear collision dynamics, strict safety constraints, and real-time computation requirements. This work presents a PIT-oriented neural optimal-control framework built around PicoPINN (Planning-Informed Compact Physics-Informed Neural Network), a compact physics-informed surrogate obtained through knowledge distillation, hierarchical parameter clustering, and relation-matrix-based parameter reconstruction. A hierarchical neural-OCP (Optimal Control Problem) architecture is then developed, in which an upper virtual decision layer generates PIT decision packages under scenario constraints and a lower coupled-MPC (Model Predictive Control) layer executes interaction-aware control. To evaluate the framework, we construct a PIT Scenario Dataset and conduct surrogate-model comparison, planning-structure ablation, and multi-fidelity assessment from simulation to scaled by-wire vehicle tests. In simulation, adding the upper planning layer improves PIT success rate from 63.8% to 76.7%, and PicoPINN reduces the original PINN parameter count from 8965 to 812 and achieves the smallest average heading error among the learned surrogates (0.112 rad). Scaled vehicle experiments are further used as evidence of control feasibility, with 3 of 4 low-speed controllable-contact PIT trials achieving successful yaw reversal.

AI.tldr: A neural optimal-control framework for automated Precision Immobilization Technique (PIT) using PicoPINN, a compact physics-informed surrogate, with hierarchical planning and control layers that improve success rates in emergency vehicle scenarios.
AI.motivation: Automating Precision Immobilization Technique (PIT) for emergency out-of-control vehicles is challenging due to highly nonlinear collision dynamics, strict safety constraints, and real-time computation requirements, necessitating an efficient control framework.
AI.method: Developed a PIT-oriented neural optimal-control framework with PicoPINN (Planning-Informed Compact Physics-Informed Neural Network) obtained through knowledge distillation, hierarchical parameter clustering, and relation-matrix-based parameter reconstruction. Uses hierarchical neural-OCP architecture with upper virtual decision layer for PIT decision packages and lower coupled-MPC layer for interaction-aware control.
AI.result: Adding upper planning layer improved PIT success rate from 63.8% to 76.7% in simulation. PicoPINN reduced PINN parameters from 8965 to 812 and achieved smallest average heading error (0.112 rad) among learned surrogates. Scaled vehicle experiments showed control feasibility with 3 of 4 low-speed controllable-contact PIT trials achieving successful yaw reversal.
AI.conclusion: The proposed neural optimal-control framework with PicoPINN effectively addresses PIT automation challenges, demonstrating improved success rates, computational efficiency, and real-world feasibility through simulation and scaled vehicle experiments.

title: Robust Nonlinear System Identification in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces via Scenario Optimization
summary: This paper proposes a method for constructing one-step prediction tubes for nonlinear systems using reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. We approximate a bounded reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) hypothesis set by a finite-dimensional subspace using bounds based on n-widths and a greedy algorithm for basis reduction. For kernels whose native spaces are norm-equivalent to Sobolev spaces, we derive how the required basis size scales with kernel smoothness and input dimension. This finite-dimensional representation enables the use of convex scenario optimization to obtain violation guarantees for the learned predictor without requiring an a priori bound on the true system's RKHS norm or Lipschitz constant. The method is demonstrated on an obstacle-avoidance task. We also discuss the main limitations of the current analysis, including dimensional scaling and dependence on i.i.d. data.

AI.tldr: Method for constructing one-step prediction tubes for nonlinear systems using RKHS approximation and convex scenario optimization with finite-dimensional representation and violation guarantees.
AI.motivation: Need for reliable prediction tubes for nonlinear systems without requiring a priori bounds on the true system's RKHS norm or Lipschitz constant, enabling safety-critical applications like obstacle avoidance.
AI.method: Approximate bounded RKHS hypothesis set by finite-dimensional subspace using n-width bounds and greedy basis reduction; use convex scenario optimization on finite-dimensional representation to obtain violation guarantees; specifically for kernels with native spaces norm-equivalent to Sobolev spaces.
AI.result: Derived scaling of required basis size with kernel smoothness and input dimension; demonstrated method on obstacle-avoidance task; obtained violation guarantees without a priori bounds on true system properties.
AI.conclusion: Method enables construction of prediction tubes with probabilistic guarantees for nonlinear systems using RKHS approximation; limitations include dimensional scaling issues and dependence on i.i.d. data assumptions.

title: From Points to Sets: Set-Based Safety Verification in the Latent Space
summary: We extend latent representation methods for safety control design to set-valued states. Recent work has shown that barrier functions designed in a learned latent space can transfer safety guarantees back to the original system, but these methods evaluate certificates at single state points, ignoring state uncertainty. A fixed safety margin can partially address this but cannot adapt to the anisotropic and time-varying nature of the uncertainty gap across different safety constraints. We instead represent the system state as a zonotope, propagate it through the encoder to obtain a latent zonotope, and evaluate certificates over the worst case of the entire set. On a 16-dimensional quadrotor suspended-load gate passage task, set-valued evaluation achieves 5/5 collision-free passages, compared to 1/5 for point-based evaluation and 2/5 for a fixed-margin baseline. Set evaluation reports safety in 44.4% of per-head evaluations versus 48.5% for point-based, and this greater conservatism detects 4.1% blind spots where point evaluation falsely certifies safety, enabling earlier corrective control. The safety gap between point and set evaluation varies up to $12\times$ across certificate heads, explaining why no single fixed margin suffices and confirming the need for per-head, per-timestep adaptation, which set evaluation provides by construction.

AI.tldr: Set-valued safety evaluation using latent zonotopes achieves better collision avoidance than point-based methods by accounting for state uncertainty across different safety constraints.
AI.motivation: Existing latent-space barrier function methods evaluate safety certificates at single state points, ignoring state uncertainty. Fixed safety margins cannot adapt to anisotropic and time-varying uncertainty gaps across different safety constraints.
AI.method: Represent system state as a zonotope, propagate it through the encoder to obtain a latent zonotope, and evaluate safety certificates over the worst case of the entire set rather than single points.
AI.result: On a 16D quadrotor suspended-load gate passage task: set-valued evaluation achieved 5/5 collision-free passages vs 1/5 for point-based and 2/5 for fixed-margin baseline. Set evaluation reports safety in 44.4% of evaluations vs 48.5% for point-based, detecting 4.1% blind spots where point evaluation falsely certifies safety.
AI.conclusion: Set evaluation provides necessary per-head, per-timestep adaptation to uncertainty gaps that vary up to 12× across certificate heads, explaining why no single fixed margin suffices and enabling earlier corrective control.

title: Local Sensitivity Analysis for Kernel-Regularized ARX Predictors in Data-Driven Predictive Control
summary: We study local sensitivity of structured ARX-based data-driven predictive control. Although predictor estimation is linear in the ARX parameters, the lifted multi-step predictor used in MPC depends on them implicitly, which complicates both uncertainty propagation and task-aware regularization. We derive a local first-order linearization of this implicit predictor map. The resulting Jacobian yields both an approximate control-relevant prediction uncertainty term and a task-dependent sensitivity metric for shaping kernel regularization. Numerical results show that the proposed analysis is most useful in weak-excitation regimes, where baseline SS regularization already provides substantial robustness gains and the proposed sensitivity shaping yields a further smaller improvement.

AI.tldr: Local sensitivity analysis of ARX-based data-driven MPC, deriving Jacobian for implicit predictor map to enable uncertainty propagation and task-aware regularization, showing benefits in weak-excitation regimes.
AI.motivation: ARX-based data-driven predictive control faces challenges with uncertainty propagation and task-aware regularization due to the implicit dependence of multi-step predictors on ARX parameters, despite linear predictor estimation.
AI.method: Derive local first-order linearization of the implicit predictor map to obtain Jacobian, enabling approximate control-relevant prediction uncertainty and task-dependent sensitivity metric for kernel regularization shaping.
AI.result: Numerical results demonstrate the analysis is most beneficial in weak-excitation regimes where baseline SS regularization already provides robustness, with sensitivity shaping offering additional smaller improvements.
AI.conclusion: The proposed local sensitivity analysis framework enables effective uncertainty propagation and task-aware regularization for ARX-based data-driven MPC, particularly valuable in low-excitation scenarios.

title: Transfer Learning for Neural Parameter Estimation applied to Building RC Models
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: Parameter estimation for dynamical systems remains challenging due to non-convexity and sensitivity to initial parameter guesses. Recent deep learning approaches enable accurate and fast parameter estimation but do not exploit transferable knowledge across systems. To address this, we introduce a transfer-learning-based neural parameter estimation framework based on a pretraining-fine-tuning paradigm. This approach improves accuracy and eliminates the need for an initial parameter guess. We apply this framework to building RC thermal models, evaluating it against a Genetic Algorithm and a from-scratch neural baseline across eight simulated buildings, one real-world building, two RC model configurations, and four training data lengths. Results demonstrate an 18.6-24.0% performance improvement with only 12 days of training data and up to 49.4% with 72 days. Beyond buildings, the proposed method represents a new paradigm for parameter estimation in dynamical systems.

AI.tldr: Transfer-learning neural framework for dynamical system parameter estimation using pretraining-fine-tuning paradigm, eliminating need for initial parameter guesses and improving accuracy.
AI.motivation: Current deep learning approaches for parameter estimation in dynamical systems don't exploit transferable knowledge across systems, and traditional methods suffer from non-convexity and sensitivity to initial parameter guesses.
AI.method: Transfer-learning-based neural parameter estimation framework using pretraining-fine-tuning paradigm, applied to building RC thermal models.
AI.result: 18.6-24.0% performance improvement with 12 days of training data, up to 49.4% with 72 days, outperforming Genetic Algorithm and from-scratch neural baseline across eight simulated buildings, one real building, two RC configurations, and four data lengths.
AI.conclusion: The method represents a new paradigm for parameter estimation in dynamical systems beyond building applications, enabling transferable knowledge exploitation and eliminating initial parameter guess requirements.

title: A note on input signal generators: A relaxation of Willems' fundamental lemma in the SISO case
summary: We provide a practical relaxation of Willems' fundamental lemma for discrete-time linear time-invariant (single-input-single-output) systems. Instead of maintaining conventional Willems' persistency of excitation condition in the behavioral theory, we reformulate the problem in terms of signal generators, hence going back to the dynamical systems theory. We discuss the relationship between the persistency of excitation order and the dimension of the signal generator. Furthermore, we identify a necessary and sufficient condition on the signal generator that can generate informative input--output data for almost all systems and initial conditions. This even includes inputs outside the class originally suggested by Willems' fundamental lemma, for example, sinusoidal sequences with fewer frequencies.
